title: US and China Agree to AI Safety Incident Notification Mechanism Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
detail: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced on September 20 that the US and China had agreed, after roughly eight hours of talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng at JPMorgan Chase's Manhattan headquarters, to establish a bilateral AI dialogue including a formal notification mechanism for AI-related incidents that rise to a national-security level — a first-of-its-kind arrangement between the two governments. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said existing US export controls on advanced AI chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment were not on the agenda and remain unchanged by the talks. The agreement, described as the most substantive AI-governance step the two countries have taken since AI competition escalated in 2022, lands four days ahead of Xi Jinping's September 24 Washington summit with President Trump, where AI governance and the expiring 90-day tariff truce are expected to be central agenda items.

media.caption: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng after talks in New York that produced the AI safety notification agreement
US and Chinese officials wrapped high-level trade and AI talks in New York ahead of the Trump-Xi summit

confidenceReason: Bessent's announcement is on the record and independently reported by CNN, NBC News and Forbes; USTR Greer's on-record clarification confirms existing chip export controls are unaffected.
